大城そば家.name: Oshiro Soba-ya
大城そば家.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop in Miyazato, Nago, marked by its salmon-pink building. The signature "Oshiro soba," where you can choose thin or flat noodles, is a very Nago-style bowl: a broth with plenty of pork bone, topped with knotted kelp.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with some additions of my own lol🍜✨ This time I'm introducing "Oshiro Soba-ya" in Miyazato, Nago.

I ate here in August 2024. This shop is close in location to "Oshiro Soba," which I introduced in "Okinawa soba shops every bit as good as my recommended shops," and the names are similar too (^0^;) I entered excitedly this time as well😊

"Oshiro Soba-ya" has the air of a place loved by locals, just from its exterior. The salmon-pink building catches the eye. At the entrance, there's an "Okinawa Soba Specialty Shop" sign and a row of wooden menu placards, which is exciting🎉

When I entered, perhaps because it was lunchtime, it was bustling with local customers. Lively voices were flying around, and you could feel the atmosphere of a popular shop. There are counter seats and table seats, and I sat at a table. (It was busy with customers, so sorry I couldn't take photos inside🙏)

Looking at the menu, the signature "Oshiro soba" jumps right out at you. Can't skip this one😆 When ordering, I was told you can choose between thin noodles and flat noodles. I tried the flat noodles, which are very Nago-like.
Meal ticket machine (at the top left is "Oshiro soba," which seems to be the recommendation)
After a while, the long-awaited "Oshiro soba" makes its appearance!🎊

First, the looks. Chunky toppings peek out of a broth gleaming golden. What's distinctive is the knotted kelp on top. This reminds me of "Miyazato Soba" in Nago, which I went to before. Maybe it's a characteristic of Nago's Okinawa soba😄
Now, as usual, I start by tasting the broth. Hm? An unexpected flavor. At first I thought it was bonito-based, but surprisingly the pork bone comes through. Just plain tasty👍
Next, the noodles. The flat noodles I chose are soft. They have a smooth, slippery texture and go fine with the broth. But personally I think I prefer a bit more bite😊

Turning to the toppings, a hefty soki sits enthroned. It's meltingly soft. When you put it in your mouth, it's soft as expected and the umami of the meat spreads gently. The seasoning is on the light side, a balanced finish that doesn't interfere with the taste of the broth.
And the knotted kelp I mentioned earlier. This makes a nice accent too. The umami of the kelp dissolves into the broth, making the overall flavor deeper.
My overall impression after eating... hmm, I'd say just plain tasty🤔 There's no particularly surprising originality, but it's reliably delicious.

Rating (9/15): It was plainly tasty, reliable Okinawa soba. It's not especially surprising like "Oshiro Soba" from "Okinawa soba shops every bit as good as my recommended shops," but I think it's a bowl you can fully enjoy as a local Nago taste. If you have a chance to come to Nago, please stop by "Oshiro Soba-ya." You're sure to spend a heartwarming time while soaking up the local atmosphere🏖️
